errors.location: Section 2, equation (2.1) and the subsequent area-preservation statement
errors.description: The stated normalization preserves area 4π only when the compact surface has Euler characteristic 2; it is not the normalized Ricci flow for an arbitrary compact surface.
errors.evidence: The text introduces an arbitrary compact surface and states that its area remains 4π under ∂t g = 2(1−K)g. Differentiating area gives dArea/dt = 2Area−2∫K dV = 8π−4πχ(M) at Area = 4π, which need not vanish.

errors.description: The displayed small-area expansion is algebraically false.
errors.evidence: The claimed equality is √(4πA−κA²) = √(4πA−κA³/(4√π)) + o(A²). The left expression is 2√π A^(1/2)−κ A^(3/2)/(4√π)+O(A^(5/2)); the right square root has no A^(3/2) term. Their difference is therefore not o(A²).

errors.location: Proposition 3.1, application of the maximum principle to the ODE solution
errors.description: The area-dependent ODE barrier is not a subsolution throughout the spatial domain, so the maximum principle does not establish the asserted bound with B(A).
errors.evidence: The proof fixes B = [A²+(4π−A)²]/[A(4π−A)] for one area and compares the resulting spatially constant f(t) with (2.5). Normal displacement changes enclosed area, so this coefficient varies with r. A subsolution requires (ln f)′ ≤ B(A(r))(1−f) everywhere; B(2π)=2, whereas B(A)>2 for A≠2π. The chosen ODE violates that inequality at the smaller coefficient.

errors.location: Theorem 3.2, the step beginning “since the inequality (2.4) is tight for A → 0”
errors.description: Asymptotic tightness does not allow the lower bound in (2.4) to replace I_A² in another lower-bound inequality; the claimed ordering is actually false for sufficiently small A under the contradiction hypothesis.
errors.evidence: The proof asserts (4πA−κ(T)A²)/(4πA−A²) ≥ 1/(1+e^(−BT−C)). For fixed T>0 and κ(T)>1, its left side is 1−(κ(T)−1)A/(4π)+O(A²). With the stated C and B(A)∼4π/A, the right side is 1−O(Ae^(−4πT/A)). Thus the left side is smaller for sufficiently small A. Knowing both quantities are lower bounds for I_A² does not order them.
